q: Which financial statement shows a company's assets, liabilities and shareholders' equity at a particular point in time?
explain: The balance sheet is a point-in-time snapshot, while the income statement and cash flow statement cover a period of time.
hook: Balance sheet = snapshot; the other two = movie.

sources.title: Three Financial Statements - Income, Balance Sheet, & Cash Flow
sources.quote: The balance sheet shows a company’s assets, liabilities, and shareholders’ equity at a particular point in time.

q: What line item is the "bottom line" of the income statement?
explain: Net income sits at the bottom of the income statement and is the starting line item of cash from operations on the cash flow statement.

sources.title: How are the Three Financial Statements Linked?
sources.quote: Net income, or the “bottom line” of the income statement, is the starting line item at the top of the cash flow statement in the cash from operations (CFO) section.

q: Under the indirect method, what is the starting line item of the cash flow statement?
explain: Net income from the income statement starts cash from operations, which then adjusts for non-cash items like D&A and changes in working capital.

sources.title: Accounting Interview Questions | Financial Statement Concepts
sources.quote: Net income on the income statement flows in as the starting line item on the cash flow statement.

sources.title: Indirect Method: Net Income to Operating Cash Flow | CFI
sources.quote: This method starts with net income and then adjusts for non-cash expenses, non-operating items, and changes in working capital.

q: Net income from the income statement flows into which balance sheet account?
explain: Net income feeds retained earnings in shareholders' equity and is also the starting point for cash from operations.

sources.title: How the 3 Financial Statements are Linked Together - Step by Step
sources.quote: On the balance sheet, it feeds into retained earnings and on the cash flow statement, it is the starting point for the cash from operations section.

sources.title: Accounting Interview Questions | Financial Statement Concepts
sources.quote: Net income flows into retained earnings in the shareholders' equity section of the balance sheet.

q: Assets equal liabilities plus what?
explain: The two sides of the balance sheet must balance: assets must equal liabilities plus equity.

sources.title: Three Financial Statements - Income, Balance Sheet, & Cash Flow
sources.quote: The two sides of the balance sheet must balance: assets must equal liabilities plus equity.

q: Capital expenditures appear in which section of the cash flow statement?
explain: Capex is a cash outflow in investing activities and adds to PP&E on the balance sheet.

sources.title: How the 3 Financial Statements are Linked Together - Step by Step
sources.quote: Capital expenditures add to the PP&E account on the balance sheet and flow through cash from investing on the cash flow statement.

sources.title: Accounting Interview Questions | Financial Statement Concepts
sources.quote: Cash Flow from Investing Activities : Captures long-term investments made by the company, primarily capital expenditures (CapEx) as well as any acquisitions or divestitures.

q: Dividends paid to shareholders are recorded as an outflow in which section of the cash flow statement?
explain: Cash from financing captures debt and equity issuances, debt repayments, share repurchases and dividends.

sources.title: Accounting Interview Questions | Financial Statement Concepts
sources.quote: Dividends paid to shareholders will also be recorded as an outflow in this section.

sources.title: How are the Three Financial Statements Linked?
sources.quote: The cash from financing (CFF) captures the inflow of cash from raising capital through debt and equity issuances, and the outflow of cash from the paydown of debt principal or the issuance of shareholder dividends.

q: The ending cash balance at the bottom of the cash flow statement flows to which balance sheet line item?
explain: Beginning cash plus the net change in cash gives ending cash, which becomes the current-period cash balance on the balance sheet.

sources.title: How are the Three Financial Statements Linked?
sources.quote: Finally, the ending cash balance at the bottom of the cash flow statement flows to the balance sheet as the cash balance for the current period.

sources.title: Three Financial Statements - Income, Balance Sheet, & Cash Flow
sources.quote: The asset section begins with cash and equivalents , which should equal the balance found at the end of the cash flow statement.

q: Ending retained earnings equals beginning retained earnings plus net income minus what?
explain: Retained earnings is the cumulative net income kept by the company after dividends to shareholders.

sources.title: Retained Earnings | Formula + Calculator
sources.quote: Retained Earnings = Beginning Retained Earnings + Net Income – Dividends

sources.title: How are the Three Financial Statements Linked?
sources.quote: The retained earnings balance in the current period is equal to the prior period’s retained earnings balance plus net income minus any dividends issued to shareholders in the current period.

q: Ending PP&E equals beginning PP&E plus capital expenditures minus what?
explain: Capex increases the PP&E balance, while depreciation reduces the recorded value of PP&E on the balance sheet.

sources.title: How are the Three Financial Statements Linked?
sources.quote: Ending PP&E = Beginning PP&E + Capital Expenditures (Capex) – Depreciation

sources.title: How the 3 Financial Statements are Linked Together - Step by Step
sources.quote: Depreciation flows out of the balance sheet from Property Plant and Equipment (PP&E) onto the income statement as an expense, and then gets added back in the cash flow statement.

q: On the cash flow statement, what is the cash effect of an increase in an operating current asset such as accounts receivable?
explain: An increase in an operating current asset is a use of cash, so it is subtracted in cash from operations.

sources.title: How are the Three Financial Statements Linked?
sources.quote: Increase in Operating Current Asset → Cash Outflow

sources.title: Indirect Method: Net Income to Operating Cash Flow | CFI
sources.quote: Subtract increases in current assets (uses of cash).

q: On the cash flow statement, what is the cash effect of an increase in an operating current liability such as accounts payable?
explain: An increase in an operating current liability is a source of cash, so it is added in cash from operations.

sources.title: How are the Three Financial Statements Linked?
sources.quote: Increase in Operating Current Liability → Cash Inflow

sources.title: Indirect Method: Net Income to Operating Cash Flow | CFI
sources.quote: Add increases in current liabilities (sources of cash).

q: Capex does not appear directly on the income statement; which expense allocates it across the asset's useful life instead?
explain: Capex increases PP&E without hitting the income statement directly; depreciation then spreads that cost over the useful life assumption.

sources.title: How are the Three Financial Statements Linked?
sources.quote: Capex increases the PP&E account on the balance sheet but does NOT appear on the income statement directly.

q: Besides D&A, which employee compensation expense is commonly added back in cash from operations as a non-cash expense?

sources.title: Indirect Method: Net Income to Operating Cash Flow | CFI
sources.quote: Stock-based compensation : Expense related to employee compensation paid in shares and is not a cash outflow.
